evidence.source: 陳家寧, 复旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心
evidence.field: abstract; graphic formation; first distinguishable forms
evidence.text: The article identifies 太 as a differentiating graph formed from 大 by adding a distinguishing dot. It reports the earliest distinguishable 太 shapes in Western Han inscriptions: 太初 on a vessel from Emperor Wu’s era and another 太初 inscription two years later. The same discussion says forms in some earlier examples proposed as 太 are disputed or read otherwise. It does not assign the added mark a semantic or phonetic function.
evidence.title: 陳家寧：說“大”、“太”和“天”的關係

evidence.source: 陳家寧, 复旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心
evidence.field: graphic development; early uses; graphic and lexical distinction
evidence.text: The author argues that pre-Qin texts used 大 for words later written 太, and that the graphic distinction developed after some meanings of 大 became distinct. The article gives parallel textual examples, such as 大子/太子 and 大山/太山, but cautions that individual 大 occurrences need contextual interpretation. It notes the Shuowen material is not a direct account of the dotted 太 graph.
evidence.title: 陳家寧：說“大”、“太”和“天”的關係

evidence.source: 葉玉英, 复旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心
evidence.field: dated degree-adverb uses in excavated sources
evidence.text: The article distinguishes the degree-adverb word from the graph used to write it. It interprets Western Zhou oracle-bone and bronze examples of 大 as degree intensification, including forms it reads as excessive degree, and reports that this word was ordinarily written 大 or sometimes 泰 in excavated materials through the Eastern Han. It cites Warring States and Qin-Han manuscripts such as Guodian Laozi, Shuihudi, Mawangdui and Zhangjiashan. These are the author’s readings and semantic classifications, not a simple graphic chronology.
evidence.title: 葉玉英：論程度副詞{太}出現的時代及其與“太”、“大”、“泰”的關係

evidence.source: 陳家寧, 复旦大学出土文献与古文字研究中心
evidence.field: sound relation; comparison of 大 and 太
evidence.text: The article describes 大 and 太 as close in sound and meaning, and discusses an initial-consonant distinction in traditional Middle Chinese categories. This is evidence for the author’s analysis of a lexical/phonological relationship; it does not make the added dot a phonetic component. No independent phonetic component within 太 is established by the inspected sources.
evidence.title: 陳家寧：說“大”、“太”和“天”的關係

search_audit.outcome: Inspected two specialist articles, the Xiaoxuetang query landing page, a government character-variant dictionary result page (detail open failed), the exact Commons 大 seal file page, and both official Unihan endpoints (both failed). The exact 太 form’s first occurrence and broader ancient form series remain supported through the paleographic article rather than direct artifact image inspection.

search_audit.query: site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File "太" Han dynasty inscription character; site:commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File "太初" Chinese inscription image
search_audit.outcome: Searches returned no directly useful, exact-file Han 太 inscription asset. Shuowen Seal Radical 389 page open failed. The usable verified image is a modern 大 seal-script rendering, relevant only as a graphic comparison.

gaps: No inspected primary artifact photograph independently verifies the article’s readings or dates for the Western Han 太初 vessel inscriptions.

The accessible evidence does not establish a unique linear semantic path from ‘big’ to ‘very/too’; excavated sources preserve overlapping uses and the specialist authors caution that manuscript dating and later transmitted-text spellings complicate chronology.

The exact origin and function of the dot are not independently demonstrated beyond its analysis as a distinguishing graphic mark; neither a person-for-scale account nor a phonetic role for 丶 is supported.
The identity and reading of several alleged pre-Han 太 forms remain disputed in the paleographic account; no image assets for those candidates were selected.
No reliable image of a dated 太 form with verified identity and reuse provenance was established. The selected comparison asset shows 大 only; it is a modern redrawing, not an ancient artifact image.

The official Unihan record endpoints for U+5927 and U+592A returned internal errors; current readings here are attributed to the supplied local rows. Local Baxter–Sagart rows were also supplied rather than independently inspected.
The Shuowen passage discussed by Chen concerns 大/亣 and 泰; it does not directly document the dotted 太 graph.
The inspected evidence does not establish graph borrowing or a depicted tool/object name underlying 太.
